about: The Marlin-2B serving version (W3): serve.sh's pinned default, verified by tests/w/test_serving.py (check_pinned_launch). `flags` is what serve.sh passes after the image on a launch with no extra arguments, with ${NAME} for the two settings. Flags a caller appends pass through to vLLM and are outside this record (a new serving version); a second value for either setting, or an --api-key, is refused, and the environment cannot change the image, --max-model-len or --gpu-memory-utilization. `engine_options_digest` is sha256 of the flags' compact JSON with `settings` substituted.

runtime_image.digest_kind: manifest list (OCI index): what a pull by `ref` resolves; on linux/amd64 it resolves to linux_amd64_manifest, whose image config is linux_amd64_config
runtime_image.resolved_by: docker buildx imagetools inspect (read-only registry call); sha256 of the raw manifest list equals the digest
runtime_image.pilot_box: meas. 2026-09-23, research/plan/evidence/w/box/inventory-20260923T0319Z.txt (SSM command 6a8569bd-e958-4a1d-9797-6496e0b12b42, 2026-09-23T03:19:48Z): image_equals_pin=yes - the running container's image id is sha256:4cbfd34aac145fd1870381c030131c7f868fcad45448f401ecdb5fd4ed020b42 (the full digest above), RepoDigests [vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:4cbfd34a...20b42], tag :nightly, created 2026-09-19T05:47:54.316012075Z, ai.vllm.build.commit a8d1aa9c99b8698a2a78b611b7a10c30e6b3995b; docker 29.7.2 with storage driver `overlayfs`. The local id there is the INDEX digest, not the amd64 config digest: `overlayfs` is Docker's name for the containerd image store's snapshotter (the classic store reports `overlay2` and would show the config digest, 38e8c0e6...) - the equality is measured, the store is read from the driver name. The box still runs the pre-pin serve.sh (by tag): same image, but its flags carry --max-num-seqs 32 and no --allowed-local-media-path until I2B's pinned deploy

settings_status.ENGINE_MAX_NUM_SEQS: ⚠️ TO BE VERIFIED: stays 8 (the pilot value, contracts limits engine_max_num_seqs). Measured 2026-09-23 (concurrency_sweep below): F(c) is never 0 - the same four 112 s clips fail at every level on the engine's encoder-cache limit (engine_limits) - so under W3's predeclared rule no level qualifies and the setting stays 8. With those deterministic failures set aside the rule would give 16 (W(c) = 0 for c <= 16; T >= 0.9 x 2.376 = 2.138 req/s first at c = 16 with 2.206; floor(X) = 80): recorded for the decision, NOT adopted. The box serves 32 and the cutover keeps 32 explicitly (I2B FC-1) until W4 resolves the encoder limit and the sweep is re-run

kv_capacity.note: the capacity is the engine's own token count, 2,644,426 (= 80.70 x 32,768). num_gpu_blocks x block_size is 2,941,408 here, NOT the capacity: this hybrid model shares the block pool between linear-attention (mamba-style) state and attention pages (the log sets the attention block to 544 so the pages match), so E1B's formula overstates it; the reason for the exact gap is not derived here

concurrency_sweep.measured: meas. 2026-09-23, E1B cell L1 by measure/concurrency.sh against the engine directly (--max-num-seqs 32, image = the pin, engine not restarted): research/plan/evidence/w/box/sweep-20260923T050411Z/ (w3-L1-20260923T050411Z.concurrency.log, w3-L1-20260923T050411Z/{bench.jsonl,c*.log,raw/,samples.tsv}); SSM launch 61273f16-5135-4fe0-90e5-97a20a4e9637; run 2026-09-23T05:04:11Z from 517e09d on the verified corpus
concurrency_sweep.protocol: closed loop, n = max(64, 4c), seed 20260922, --max-tokens 128,512,1024, --subset full, --engine-state warm, video_b64
concurrency_sweep.labels: rows from bench.py --report; its per-cell limits apply (p99 suppressed below 300 samples; P-18 criteria are provisional, not targets); peak_* from the 2 s samples; peak_waiting printed empty for c = 1..16 is 0, and the 2 at c = 32 was scraped with a prefix match that also counted num_requests_waiting_by_reason (fixed after the run), so the true peak may be 1
concurrency_sweep.failures: every failure is one of the four 112 s clips (c012, c025, c038, c051): 4 per level, 8 at c = 32 (each clip twice), 28 in total; bench: stream_error_event, platform-attributed
concurrency_sweep.rule: W3's predeclared rule (evidence): c* = smallest c with F(c) = 0, W(c) = 0, T(c) >= 0.9 max T; ENGINE_MAX_NUM_SEQS = min(c*, floor(X)), X = 80.70 (kv_capacity). Literal result: no level qualifies (F > 0 everywhere). Conditional result with the 112 s clips set aside: 16 (not adopted)

engine_limits.measured: meas. 2026-09-23 in the sweep (concurrency_sweep): the four 112 s clips are rejected at every level with `VLLMValidationError: video item with 20160|21168|21504 embedding tokens exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 16384` (the engine's start-up: encoder cache budget of 16384 tokens, profiled with 1 image item) - the error text and the start-up line are quoted from the coordinator record (the engine log), the clip ids, durations and counts from the committed raw/; the longest accepted clip is 72 s (c024, 14,773 prompt tokens)
engine_limits.client_view: HTTP 200, then an SSE error event about 9 s later
engine_limits.consequence: ⚠️ this engine configuration rejects clips the API admits (contracts limits max_video_seconds 120): a deterministic configuration limit, not a load effect. W4 decides (raise the encoder budget, lower the admitted length, or pre-reject at admission) with a re-measurement; until then G2's validation has pending input P-20 (a temporary cap at the longest accepted length, 72 s, or an explicit W4 setting)
